week.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
week.readme: AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Agents don't fit the request/response model. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent.

new.readme: XCL is a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) games you own on a Windows PC - in the spirit of Wine/Proton. There is no CPU emulation: the game's x64 code runs natively, and XCL provides its own, independently written implementations of the console system libraries the PC does not have (kernelx.dll, XGameRuntime, d3d12xs.dll, …). The console's GPU code (RDNA2 machine code) is recompiled into PC shaders (HLSL → DXIL).

new.description: XNU as a loadable kernel module inside Linux (macOS personality for arm64 Linux)
new.readme: Run macOS userspace on Linux by loading the macOS kernel into it. xnulinux builds XNU, the open-source kernel of macOS, from Apple's published sources and runs it as a loadable kernel module (xnu.ko) inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel. The hosted XNU drives the CPU and MMU directly, so macOS processes run natively next to Linux processes on the same CPUs, with no hypervisor between them. Linux lends XNU its memory, timers, files, network and GPU through a small interface module (fki.ko).

items.title: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors
items.harder: Overseas data centers that remotely supply significant compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau face new export restrictions, and chip exporters, foundries and data centers must perform due diligence on customers.
items.quote: These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models.
items.who: Overseas data centers, foreign foundries, chip exporters, and D:5 or Macau headquartered firms
items.why: Cloud compute providers abroad must now screen customer ownership and control before supplying large volumes of compute built on U.S. chips.
items.limits: Interim final rule open for comment; thresholds for significant compute volumes not stated in the summary
